10.1002_adma.75568: Eliminating Co from ultrahigh‐Ni layered cathodes often exacerbates Li/Ni mixing, impeding Li + transport, amplifying reaction heterogeneity, and accelerating structural degradation. Most strategies focus on minimizing the overall degree of cation mixing, whereas thermodynamic control of antisite spatial organization remains underexplored. Here, we address this central stability challenge by developing a thermodynamics‐guided defect‐engineering strategy that stabilizes spatially correlated Li/Ni antisite configurations in cobalt‐free ultrahigh‐Ni cathodes. Density functional theory screening of high‐valence dopants reveals that Te 6+ exhibits the strongest energetic preference for spatially correlated antisite configurations. This prediction guides the synthesis of LiNi 0.948 Al 0.045 Te 0.007 O 2 containing coherent local antisite‐ordered superlattice domains. These ordered domains persist after prolonged cycling, strengthen interlayer coupling, suppress H2–H3 phase separation and c ‐axis contraction, and preserve low‐barrier Li + migration pathways. Local Te–O coordination further stabilizes lattice oxygen and mitigates oxygen‐loss‐induced surface reconstruction. Consequently, the cathode delivers 185 mAh g −1 at 10 C, retains 96.7% of its initial capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C with a 4.4 V cutoff, and retains 92% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles with a 4.6 V cutoff. These findings establish the spatial organization of defects as a critical design variable for mitigating the stability‐transport trade‐off in cobalt‐free ultrahigh‐Ni layered cathodes.
10.1002_aenm.71322: This study presents a novel electrochemical hydrogenation (EH‐DPM) system that integrates clean hydrogen production and storage by utilizing a diphenylmethane (H0‐DPM, DPM) /dicyclohexylmethane (H12‐DPM, DCM) pair as a liquid organic hydrogen carrier (LOHC). The system operates in a full‐cell configuration, coupling a cathode for the electrochemical hydrogenation of H0‐DPM (EH‐DPM) with a proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) anode, thereby enabling direct hydrogen storage in the LOHC during water splitting. The EH‐DPM system demonstrates higher energy efficiency than conventional PEMWE, achieving reaction currents at lower potentials. A comparative testing of Pt and Ru black electrocatalysts reveals that Ru black outperforms Pt black at higher voltages (> 1.5 V), achieving significantly higher selectivity (92.3% at 1.6 V) for the fully hydrogenated H12‐DPM. 1 H‐NMR and 13 C‐NMR analyses identifies cyclohexylmethylbenzene (H6‐DPM, CMB) as the sole hydrogenation intermediate, highlighting that optimal electrocatalyst selection is crucial for maximizing H12‐DPM yield and minimizing energy losses from intermediate formation. Density functional theory calculations elucidate catalyst‐dependent reaction pathways and show that distinct hydrogen migration barriers on Pt and Ru surfaces account for the observed voltage‐dependent selectivity. These findings suggest that Ru black is a promising electrocatalyst for developing commercially viable hydrogen storage technologies based on the EH‐DPM system.
10.1002_anie.202504815: Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 − RR) to ammonia (NH 3 ) offers a sustainable route for NH₃ synthesis and environmental remediation, yet it is hindered by sluggish kinetics due to inefficient proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) processes and inadequate electrocatalyst design. Conventional approaches primarily focus on the bulk electronic modulation of the electrocatalyst while neglecting interfacial water dynamics. Here, we propose a dual‐functional sulfur‐doping strategy in Co 3 O 4 (S‐Co 3 O 4 ) to simultaneously enhance bulk conductivity and optimize interfacial proton transfer. Through innovative benzene sulfonyl chloride blocking experiment, in situ spectroscopic analyses, and kinetic isotope effect studies, we reveal that sulfur doping narrows the bandgap of Co 3 O 4 to enhance bulk charge transport while disrupting rigid hydrogen‐bond network of water in the electric double layer; the weakly hydrogen‐bonded H 2 O reduces the dissociation barrier and facilitates proton supply for nitrate hydrogenation. The proposed “electronic‐interfacial synergy” strategy establishes a transformative paradigm for designing electrocatalysts in PCET‐driven reactions, advancing sustainable energy conversion and environmental applications.
10.1002_smll.72883: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have attracted tremendous attention due to their ultrahigh energy density. However, fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), a commonly used additive in traditional ester‐based electrolytes, is usually over‐reduced during cycling, leading to form an extra‐thick solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) which hinders the transport of Li + and deteriorates fast charging performance. Herein, we propose a decomposition‐competition‐driven strategy to control the growth of SEI. Acetonitrile (AN) preferentially decompose to form a nitrogen‐containing SEI due to low Lowest Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (LUMO) energy level (−2.96 eV), high polarity, and favorable wettability, which exhibits a capacity of inhibiting the decomposition of FEC. As a result, the polarization voltage of the cell is remarkably stable. Furthermore, AN reconstructs the solvation structure, accelerates Li + desolvation and increases the Li + transference number and diffusion coefficient. Benefiting from the optimized electrolyte system, Li||Li cells demonstrate stable cycling over 3300 h at 1 mA cm − 2 , and Li||LFP cells retain 155 mAh g − 1 after 500 cycles at 1 C with 91.57% capacity retention. Additionally, excellent rate and long‐cycle performance can also be achieved in high‐voltage Li||NCM811 cells. This work provides new insights into enhancing interfacial and transport properties of electrolytes for practical LMBs.
10.1016_j.isci.2025.111748: Efficient photosynthesis using CO 2 and photovoltaics is an attractive solution to address environmental and energy crises. However, most attempts toward solar-driven CO 2 conversion have focused on producing fuels such as CO, CH 4 , and ethanol by CO 2 electroreduction. Here, we demonstrate the efficient electrocarboxylation of CO 2 with 1,4-dibromobenzene (1,4-DBB) to value-added carboxylic acid esters driven solely by simulated sunlight. Employing a series-connected dye-sensitized photovoltaic and a silver (Ag) catalyst electrode with outstanding performance, a Faraday efficiency (FE) of 45.6% is achieved, which is close to the 47.7% FE of the common CO 2 electrocarboxylation reaction. After 14 h, the FE of the whole photoelectrochemical system is still 66% of the initial FE. In addition, a stacking-separating strategy was adopted to assemble a series-connected dye-sensitized solar cell (DSC) module, which was flexibly assembled and easily detachable. This study offers a promising approach to producing value-added carboxylic acid derivatives from solar light and CO 2 .
10.1016_j.jece.2026.124782: The growing demand for sustainable energy necessitates efficient and cost-effective electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), a crucial step in the production of green hydrogen. While platinum (Pt) is highly efficient, its scarcity and high-cost limit large-scale application. Herein, an economically viable and environmentally friendly preparation strategy is proposed for constructing metallic nanoparticles (NPs: Pt, Ag, and Fe) on a carbon black (CB) support. Metallic NPs were green-synthesized, without volatile or toxic organic solvents, using aqueous extracts of Paullinia cupana (guaraná) and Coffea arabica (coffee husk) as both reducing and stabilizing agents. Morphological, structural, and spectroscopic analyses (XRD, SEM, EDS, UV-Vis) confirmed the successful formation of nanoparticles with good dispersion and purity. Among the nanocomposites evaluated, the Pt/CB electrode achieved the lowest overpotential, 70.9 mV, at a current density of 10 mA cm-2 and the highest exchange current density for HER. When evaluating accelerated aging tests, the Ag/CB electrode exhibited remarkable resistance to degradation. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) further supported these findings, indicating that the Ag/CB electrode retained relatively stable electronic properties even after aging, suggesting their viability for long-term applications. This approach, which leverages agro-industrial waste and environmentally benign methods, aligns with the principles of green chemistry and the circular economy, offering a promising route for the sustainable development of electrocatalysts for the generation of green hydrogen.
10.1021_acsami.6c01995: Photoresponsive surfaces are attracting increasing interest, particularly because their physicochemical properties can be selectively and temporally controlled by a noninvasive stimulus. However, photoresponsive moieties are also known to respond to other stimuli, some of which are well-studied (e.g., temperature and pH), while others are less understood. This work presents the first demonstration of a combined photochemical and electrocatalytic response of azo-based molecular photoswitches embedded in self-assembled monolayers, revealing a previously unrecognized functional synergy that yields electrochromic behavior potentially suitable for optoelectronic applications. The molecular design facilitates catalytic electrochemical switching, allowing for the transition of the photoswitches between three different states and enabling electrocatalytic control over Z to E azo bond isomerization. Ultimately, the coupling of photo- and electrochemical responses in self-assembled monolayers may eventually enable molecular synapses for application in neuromorphic nanoelectronics and molecular electronics.
10.1021_acsenergylett.5c03404: Fluorinated solvents and gel electrolytes offer potential for safe sodium-ion batteries (SIBs); yet, conventional acrylate gels show polarity mismatch, poor compatibility, and sluggish Na + transport. Here, we develop an all-fluorinated gel electrolyte by introducing a low-surface-energy perfluorinated acrylate monomer (PFHEA) into an FEMC/TFPC system. The −C 8 F 17 chains enable polarity matching and uniform gelation, improving wettability, reducing interfacial resistance, and restructuring the Na + solvation environment. Molecular dynamics and spectroscopic results indicate enhanced contact-ion pair formation and fluorine-rich SEI/CEI layers, boosting transport kinetics, interfacial stability, and thermal tolerance. Consequently, 2.6 Ah NCFM||HC pouch cells retain 88.1% capacity after 2600 cycles at 25 °C─representing 2–3-fold longer lifetimes than previously reported Ah-level Na pouch cells. A 115 Ah pouch cell further exhibits a negligible temperature rise during nail penetration, confirming intrinsic flame retardancy. This PFHEA-based gel provides a feasible route toward safe SIBs.
10.1038_s41467-026-75032-6: Dual-atom catalysts (DACs) hold significant promise for advanced oxidation processes. However, their practical application is often limited by sluggish electron transfer and low atomic utilization efficiency. Herein, we report that P-bridged Fe-Cu bimetallic catalysts (FeCu-NP-C) were precisely modulated by first-shell N and P ligands, forming a unique N 3 Fe-P 1 -CuN 3 structure. The Fe-P-Cu bridging bond induced d-p-d gradient orbital coupling to establish a directional electron-transfer channel from the Cu site (electron donor) to the Fe site (electron acceptor) for enabling ultrafast pollutant degradation and bacterial inactivation. FeCu-NP-C activated peroxymonosulfate to selectively generate high-valent iron-oxo species at a concentration of 5.80 × 10 − 5 mM, which was 100 times higher than that of Fe-NP-C. Remarkably, the FeCu-NP-C membrane reactor achieved a treatment capacity of 500 L of wastewater per gram of catalyst over 100 h, at an operational cost of US$0.055 per ton. This work provides deep insights into the bridge-mediated orbital interactions of DACs for water decontamination.
10.1039_d4ta07674e: The crystal graph convolutional neural networks predict stable Ag–Pd–F catalysts for the formate oxidation reaction from Materials Project data with DFT verifying their thermodynamic, dynamic stability and catalytic activity.
10.1109_tte.2026.3707512: The performance of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) deteriorates at low temperatures, impacting the popularization of electric vehicles (EVs). A promising solution is integrating self-heating circuits into the motor drive system of battery packs. Current schemes require the motor rotor to be pre-aligned to a specific angle to fully utilize the current-carrying capacity of the winding as well as to avoid torque generation, which is impractical in real vehicles due to the absence of a clutch. This article introduces a novel design that connects the motor’s neutral conductor to a capacitor. During heating, the inverter is controlled such that the three-phase windings of the motor carry currents of identical magnitudes and directions. This configuration not only increases the current-carrying capacity but also eliminates torque generation without needing to pre-adjust the rotor. Experimental analysis confirms that the system operates with zero motor torque irrespective of the rotor’s angle. In addition, an equivalent mathematical model and a new low-temperature heating control strategy are developed. Experiments validate the model’s accuracy and the reliability of the heating strategy. For 18650 lithium-ion batteries, the temperature rise rate at an SOC of 0.2 can reach$6.279~^{\circ }$C/min, with a corresponding energy loss of 0.125% SOC/°C. Compared to existing methods, this approach does not require rotor angle adjustment in advance, offers high heating efficiency, and maintains low energy consumption.
